methodology_note: Re-scored under revised rubric v2 by meta-agent (Claude Code) as single evaluator. Automated 3-judge sessions remain unfixed. Calibration: 2 = competent, 3 = genuinely impressive, 4 = exceptional.

scores.engine_reasoning: Has approximate timelines (90 days, 1 year) and mechanism names (harnesses, policy gates, incident-to-eval loops), but no named companies, no specific dates, no quantitative thresholds. Meets '2' anchor: approximate timelines without named actors.
scores.baseline_reasoning: Names companies (Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor, Cognition/Devin, Aider, Cline, Continue, OpenHands) and has phased timelines (0-3m, 3-6m, 6-12m, 'by late 2026'), plus one threshold (20-30%). But actors appear as a group list, not making individual dated predictions. Does not tightly couple named actors + specific timelines + mechanisms for a 3.
scores.engine_evidence: "By 90 days... By 1 year"; mechanisms: "incident-to-eval loops," "policy evaluation," "staged rollout"
scores.baseline_evidence: "Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor, Cognition/Devin, Aider, Cline, Continue, and OpenHands-class systems"; "By late 2026"; "20-30% of engineering tasks"

scores.engine_reasoning: 2-3 original insights: 'capital-goods market' analogy, 'selection capital' framing, vendor overclaiming creating misleading equilibrium, layered industrial organization with biology analogy. These go beyond the input but don't reframe the domain. Under strict calibration, solid 2.
scores.baseline_reasoning: Similar level: safety-liveness asymmetry as decisive, portfolio optimization framing, private memory as moat. 'What Might Surprise' adds some challenge insights. Multiple insights but none introduce a novel framework that reframes the domain. Solid 2.
scores.engine_evidence: "the domain is maturing into a capital-goods market"; "conceptual premature closure"; "selection capital"
scores.baseline_evidence: "safety-liveness asymmetry is decisive"; "managed selection pipelines with memory: candidate portfolios"; "bounded portfolio optimization"

scores.engine_reasoning: Predictions are stated as assertions or trends: 'selection quality remained scarcer than generation quality,' 'governed mutation pipelines outperformed.' None include falsification criteria. Some could in principle be checked but most are too vague to evaluate definitively. Score: 1.
scores.baseline_reasoning: Several predictions include 'Would increase if... Would decrease if...' conditions that name observable changes. Not explicit 'if X hasn't happened by [date], this is wrong' but clear enough to evaluate after the fact. The Confidence Levels section systematically provides checkable conditions for each prediction. Score: 2.
scores.engine_evidence: No falsification conditions. Predictions: "broad autonomous product evolution did not become production-grade" — evaluable but not falsifiable with criteria
scores.baseline_evidence: "Would decrease if frontier agents begin reliably shipping multi-service product changes with minimal scaffolding"; "Would increase if more platform-engineering case studies show successful generated workflows under policy"

scores.engine_reasoning: Covers ~6 themes: generation vs selection, governance, enterprise adoption, vendor dynamics, industrial organization, biology/economics analogies. Themes are connected (selection capital + governance + industrial org) but coverage is not comprehensive. Score: 2.
scores.baseline_reasoning: Covers 11+ themes: generation vs selection, governance/policy, enterprise adoption, vendor dynamics, formal methods, multi-agent coordination, benchmark vs trust gap, typed vs untyped environments, private memory/telemetry, portfolio optimization, organizational politics/approvals. Cross-theme interactions explicit across temporal phases and direction counterfactuals. Under strict calibration, genuinely impressive breadth with coherent system. Score: 3.
scores.engine_evidence: Themes: "governed mutation pipelines," "industrial organization," "selection capital," "capital-goods market," vendor overclaiming
scores.baseline_evidence: Adds themes not in engine: "Formal methods do not become universal"; "Multi-agent systems remain coordination-heavy"; "Typed and strongly verified environments"; "portfolio management of candidate solutions"

scores.engine_reasoning: Most claims grounded in mechanisms. Uncertainty signaled through practitioner/critic/adjacent-domain disagreement framing. But no explicit confidence levels attached to individual predictions. Meets 2: 'Most claims reference mechanisms or evidence; some explicit uncertainty.'
scores.baseline_reasoning: Claims grounded in mechanisms AND includes explicit confidence levels (high/medium/medium-high) for each key finding. States what would change confidence up or down. Meets 3: 'Claims grounded in named signals or evidence with explicit confidence levels and stated assumptions.' Under strict calibration, genuinely impressive — systematic confidence tracking.
scores.engine_evidence: "This architecture is technically feasible now because each component is already maturing independently"; uncertainty via three-probe disagreement
scores.baseline_evidence: Every key finding has "Confidence: high/medium"; systematic "Would increase if... Would decrease if..." for each prediction

scores.engine_reasoning: Two time points (90 days, 1 year) mentioned in executive summary: 'By 90 days... By 1 year, that pattern intensified.' But the predictions within each timeframe are essentially snapshots — the 1-year point repeats and amplifies the 90-day observations rather than building causally. No phase-by-phase breakdown. Score: 1.
scores.baseline_reasoning: Explicit 3-phase structure (0-3m, 3-6m, 6-12m) with 'Causal links to next phase' sections. Phase 2 builds on Phase 1's substrate ('once teams have evals, traces, and approval logic'). Clear development across phases. But later phases don't revise or falsify earlier predictions — they extend them. Score: 2.
scores.engine_evidence: "By 90 days, the center of gravity had already moved... By 1 year, that pattern intensified" — development is amplification not transformation
scores.baseline_evidence: "This phase creates the substrate for the next step: once teams have evals, traces, and approval logic, they can begin to safely compare multiple generated variants"

scores.engine_reasoning: 4 decision-point bullets are recommendations without triggers, options, or tradeoffs: 'Invest first in...', 'Track...', 'Treat... as a strategic metric', 'Avoid equating...' These are vague implications, not conditional recommendations. Score: 1.
scores.baseline_reasoning: 4 full decision points with timing triggers ('When more than 20-30% of engineering tasks involve coding agents'), 3 options each (A/B/C), and tradeoffs per option. But tradeoffs lack concrete cost quantification ('A is cheapest short term but creates fragile, non-compounding usage' — what does 'cheapest' mean in dollars or headcount?). Score: 2.
scores.engine_evidence: "Invest first in repo- and service-specific harness coverage"; "Track verified changes per review hour"
scores.baseline_evidence: "When more than 20-30% of engineering tasks involve coding agents"; Options A/B/C; "A is cheapest short term but creates fragile, non-compounding usage"

scores.engine_reasoning: Clear narrative with good structure (Executive Summary, Key Findings, Active Directions, Decision Points, Methodology). A VP could understand the findings. But the 'so what' requires extraction — no single prioritized recommendation, no deadline, no quantified tradeoff. Score: 2.
scores.baseline_reasoning: Also well-structured with more comprehensive sections. Executive summary is informative but doesn't open with THE one decision, name a deadline, or quantify the tradeoff. Decision points are presented with equal weight, not prioritized. A VP would understand it but would need to extract the top action. Score: 2.
scores.engine_evidence: Clear headings and polished prose, but Decision Points are unprioritized bullets
scores.baseline_evidence: 4 decision frameworks but no prioritization signal; executive summary describes landscape rather than leading with a decision

scores.engine_reasoning: Identifies genuine tensions: 'the field has improved selection infrastructure without solving the measurement problem required for true directed evolution.' Warns of 'conceptual premature closure' and vendor overclaiming. More than token caveats — identifies fragile assumptions. But doesn't make explicit contradictory predictions with formatted evidence. Score: 2.

'Better models automatically produce viable directed evolution' — overturned using the graph's own safety-liveness asymmetry. 'Human approvals are temporary friction' — contradicted with 'they encode real accountability, regulatory boundaries, and political legitimacy.' Meets 3: specific predictions contradicting the source, with evidence from the source itself.
scores.engine_evidence: "the field has improved selection infrastructure without solving the measurement problem required for true directed evolution"; "conceptual premature closure"
scores.baseline_evidence: "Better models automatically produce viable directed evolution" challenged; "Human approvals are temporary friction" contradicted with institutional evidence from the graph
